question: During the teenage growth spurt, which part of the body experiences a massive doubling in mass?
explanation: Spot on! Bone growth speeds up like crazy during puberty, causing a teen's skeletal mass to roughly double. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why do teenage boys and girls need different nutritional care during puberty?

options.A: Girls stop growing in height much earlier than boys do.
options.B: Boys develop more lean muscle while girls accumulate more body fat.
options.C: Girls require virtually no extra protein during puberty.
options.D: Boys have higher vitamin requirements than any other demographic.

explanation: That's correct! Puberty hormones push boys to build more muscle and bone, while girls naturally store a bit more body fat to support future reproductive needs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the main job of dietary calcium during the teenage years?
explanation: Spot on! The teenage years are the golden window where most of your adult bone strength is locked in. Drink up that milk! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h2)

question: A 14-year-old girl who has recently started menstruating is at a higher risk for running low on which nutrient?
explanation: You got it! Monthly period blood loss combined with rapid body growth means she needs extra iron to keep her energy up and prevent anemia. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h2)

question: What tool do healthcare workers mainly use to check if children and teens (ages 2 to 20) are underweight or carrying excess weight?

options.D: Standard adult body mass index tables

explanation: Correct! Because kids and teens are still growing, we use special age- and sex-matched charts instead of standard adult tables to see how they're doing. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h3)

question: As a nurse, why should you look at growth trends over time rather than just a single weight check?

options.A: A single measurement cannot show whether a teen is following their expected growth curve.
options.B: Single measurements are legally invalid for minors in healthcare settings.
options.C: Scales in clinics are rarely calibrated for adolescent body weights.
options.D: Weight changes too slowly to be measured during a routine annual checkup.

explanation: Spot on! Checking weight across multiple visits helps you spot sudden jumps or drops that might signal a health or nutrition issue. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which sign is a classic clue that a teenager might be dealing with iron deficiency anemia?

options.C: Yellowing of the skin and eyes

explanation: Correct! Low iron means less hemoglobin to carry oxygen around the body, leaving the teen feeling constantly wiped out and tired. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why do so many teenagers today end up low on vitamin D?

options.A: Consuming too many citrus fruits and juices
options.B: Drinking excessive amounts of plain water
options.C: Avoiding all forms of dietary protein
options.D: Spending less time outdoors in natural sunlight

explanation: You nailed it! Our bodies make vitamin D from sunlight on the skin. With more indoor time and screen sessions, teens get less natural sun exposure. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical behavioral warning sign of an eating disorder in a teenager?

options.A: Obsessive preoccupation with calorie counting and food labels
options.B: Eating large balanced meals happily with family every evening
options.C: Wearing oversized clothing to hide noticeable weight loss
options.D: Frequent trips to the bathroom immediately following meals

explanation: Spot on! Teens with eating disorders usually avoid family dinners or hide their eating habits, rather than happily enjoying big meals with everyone. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why are teenagers so vulnerable to feeling bad about their body image?

options.A: Hormonal imbalances permanently destroy a teenager's self-esteem.
options.B: Rapid physical changes collide with intense social pressure and peer comparison.
options.C: Schools mandate strict physical fitness testing that lowers morale.
options.D: Teenagers naturally lose the ability to regulate their emotional responses.

explanation: True! Puberty brings fast, obvious changes that teens often compare against unrealistic social media standards and their peers. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h5)

question: A teenager living with chronic obesity faces a much higher risk of developing which condition early in life?
explanation: You got it! Extra body fat makes the body struggle with insulin, putting teens with obesity at a higher risk for type 2 diabetes. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is a great, simple first step a nurse can suggest to an overweight teenager looking to improve their diet?

options.A: Replace sugary sodas and packaged drinks with water.
options.B: Consume only liquid protein shakes until target weight is met.
options.C: Eliminate all carbohydrates from daily meals completely.
options.D: Fast for two full days every week to jumpstart weight loss.

explanation: Spot on! Swapping out sugary drinks for water cuts down on empty liquid calories easily without driving the teen toward unhealthy crash diets. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why is a pregnant teenager at a much higher risk for nutritional shortages than an adult pregnant woman?

options.A: She is still growing herself and must compete with the fetus for nutrients.
options.B: Adult women require half the daily calories of teenagers.
options.C: Her digestive tract is shorter and absorbs fewer vitamins overall.
options.D: Hormones during teen pregnancy completely block fat digestion.

explanation: Correct! The teen's body is still finishing its own growth spurt while also feeding a growing baby, creating a huge demand for extra nutrients. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h7)

question: Which vitamin is especially important in early pregnancy to help prevent neural tube defects in the baby?
explanation: You nailed it! Folate (or folic acid) is vital during the early weeks of pregnancy to help the baby's brain and spinal cord form properly. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h7)

question: What is usually the main problem with lecturing teenagers about making poor food choices?

options.A: It makes them feel judged and causes them to withdraw from counseling.
options.B: Lectures cause an immediate drop in their blood glucose levels.
options.C: It legally violates their medical privacy rights.
options.D: Teens lack the brain development required to understand nutrition.

explanation: Spot on! Teens hate feeling judged. A friendly, supportive chat builds way more trust than an old-school lecture. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h8)

question: Which counseling approach works best when you want to help a teenager change their eating habits?

options.A: Handing them a strict, unchangeable 1,500-calorie diet chart
options.B: Directing their parents to control all food brought into the home
options.C: Asking open-ended questions to let the teen set personal goals
options.D: Warning them about future diseases until they agree to comply

explanation: You got it! Giving teens a voice and letting them choose their own goals makes them much more motivated to stick with healthy changes. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h8)
